blocks.text: JAMES, PETER & JUDE · THE WRITER · THE WRITER · THE WRITER · THE FAMILY
The writers
Who wrote them: James and Jude, brothers of Jesus, and the apostle Peter; then the family they came from.
THE WRITER
James, the Lord's brother
James's life in the story, step by step. His own page has the rest.
1 Named among Jesus' brothers at Nazareth
2 The brothers do not yet believe in him
3 The risen Jesus is seen by James
4 The brothers gather with the disciples
5 Paul meets "James the Lord's brother" in Jerusalem
6 Freed from prison, Peter says "Go shew these things unto James"
7 James gives the deciding speech at the Jerusalem meeting
8 Paul reports to James on his last visit to Jerusalem
9 The letter of James

The steps follow the order of the New Testament story; they are a sequence, not dates. Paul also names James as one of the three "pillars" of the Jerusalem church (Galatians 2:9). Where the letter falls in it depends on which James wrote it and when — both disputed. Jerome says James led the Jerusalem church for thirty years, until the seventh year of Nero. Galatians 2:9 [13][1]
James's own page
THE WRITER
Peter, the apostle
Peter's life in the story, step by step. His own page has the rest.
1 A Bethsaida fisherman, brought to Jesus by Andrew and named Cephas
2 Called from his nets to become a fisher of men
3 Confesses Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God
4 With James and John at the Transfiguration
5 Denies knowing Jesus three times
6 The risen Lord appears to him, then bids him: "Feed my sheep"
7 Preaches to the crowds at Pentecost
8 Brings the gospel to the centurion Cornelius and his household
9 Paul names him a pillar, then opposes him at Antioch
10 Writes to believers scattered across Asia Minor
11 By tradition, crucified at Rome under Nero

The steps follow the order of the New Testament story, not dates, from the Galilean fisherman to the letter to Asia Minor; Jesus foretells the manner of Peter's death (John 21:18–19), but that it came at Rome under Nero is later tradition, as Eusebius reports it, and is labelled so. John 21:18–19 [10][11]
Peter's own page
THE WRITER
Jude, the Lord's brother
Jude's life in the story, step by step. His own page has the rest.
1 Named among Jesus' brothers at Nazareth
2 The brothers do not yet believe in him
3 The brothers gather in prayer with the apostles
4 The Lord's brothers travel with their wives; Mayor counts Jude among them
5 Writes as "brother of James" (Mayor, Bigg and the ISBE take him for the Lord's brother; others doubt it)
6 By tradition, his grandsons are questioned by the emperor Domitian

The steps follow the order of the New Testament story, not dates, and most speak of the Lord's brothers as a group; the last comes from Hegesippus as Eusebius reports it, and is labelled as tradition.[11]
Jude's own page
THE FAMILY
The family of Jesus
The family of Jesus, as the Gospels and the letters name them.
Jesus mother "brother" "brother" "brother" FAMILY Mark 6:3 Matthew 13:55 Galatians 1:19
Mary mother FAMILY Mark 6:3 Matthew 13:55

James "The Lord's brother" (Gal 1:19), leader of the Jerusalem church; linked with the letter of James. "brother" "brother of James" (if he is the Jude of the letter) BROTHERS Mark 6:3 Matthew 13:55 Galatians 1:19 +1 more
Joses "brother" BROTHERS Mark 6:3 Matthew 13:55

Juda (Judas) "Juda" in Mark, "Judas" in Matthew. Whether he is the Jude of the letter is a separate question. "brother" "brother of James" (if he is the Jude of the letter) grandfather BROTHERS Mark 6:3 Matthew 13:55 Jude 1:1
Simon "brother" BROTHERS Mark 6:3 Matthew 13:55
Jude's grandsons Brought before the emperor Domitian and released, as Eusebius tells it from Hegesippus. grandfather LATER

Mark and Matthew name four "brethren" of Jesus: James, Joses, Juda (Judas) and Simon. The relationship has been read three ways — as younger children of Joseph and Mary (the Helvidian view), as sons of Joseph by an earlier wife (the Epiphanian view), or as cousins (the Hieronymian view, after Jerome). The lines here say only "brother", as the text does. Mark 6:3 Matthew 13:55 [1][11]
